translation_notes: no island applies: translated.ldpy is byte-identical to original.py (ldpy is a superset of Python, so the region is already a valid ldpy program with unchanged meaning); the driver still exercises both sides, which checks that the transpiler passes the region through unaltered

negative finding: all four RDF operations are I/O - two Graph() constructors and two Graph.parse(data=..., format='ttl') calls over Turtle text read from a file and produced by yatter.translate(). The RDF is never written in the program text, so islands have nothing to bind to

negative finding: R2RML_URI = 'http://www.w3.org/ns/r2rml#' is an IRI but is passed as yatter's mapping_format *string* and string-compared inside yatter; writing it as the island <http://www.w3.org/ns/r2rml#> would silently change its runtime type from str to URIRef, so it is deliberately left as a Python string
